chunks: And Al-Ala' narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then write [a contract of emancipation] for them if you know any good in them.' He said: 'The 'good' is that he bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that he possesses a skill by which he can earn a livelihood or has a trade.'

key_terms.خَيْرًا: Good (in the context of the verse, referring to capability and faith)

ai.seo_question: What does 'good' mean in the context of freeing a slave according to Imam al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that the 'goodness' (khayran) required for a mukataba contract entails both theological correctness—specifically the testimony of faith (shahada)—and practical economic viability through a trade. This dual criterion ensures the slave is not only spiritually aligned but also financially capable of fulfilling the manumission agreement, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on combining faith with actionable competence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3491 - Al-Ala' narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic:
"Then write [a contract of emancipation] for them if you know any good in them" (Surah An-Nur 24:33).
Imam (as) said: "The 'good' refers to bearing witness that there is no god but Allah (swt) and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (swt), and that the slave possesses a skill by which he can earn a livelihood or has a trade."
